title: Marrow Studio
description:
Marrow Studio is a minimalist marketing website for an independent Indian branding and web design agency, built as a synthesis of editorial design
  sensibility and modern web engineering. The visual language centers on a "warm mineral" palette—Bone White backgrounds, Charcoal Slate text, and a
  restrained Terracotta Vermilion accent occupying under 10% of visual weight—paired with a deliberate typographic hierarchy: Instrument Serif for editorial
  headlines, DM Sans for clean body copy, and JetBrains Mono for precise meta-labels. Architected on Next.js 14 with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, the App
  Router powers a mobile-first, fully responsive experience featuring dynamic project case studies, a work gallery, and a validated contact form backed by
  an API route. Every page includes comprehensive SEO metadata, Open Graph tags, and JSON-LD structured data, while next/image ensures optimized media
  delivery. The codebase targets 90+ scores across all Lighthouse categories—Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO—reflecting a commitment to
  technical rigor matching the studio's design standards. The result is a performant, accessible, and visually cohesive digital storefront that communicates
  the agency's expertise through both its content and its craft.

title: Nilgiri House
description:
A production-ready marketing and booking-enquiry website for a fictional 6-room boutique hotel in the Nilgiri hills of South India. Built
  as a portfolio piece demonstrating client-handoff-ready websites where non-technical editors control all content through Sanity CMS.

  Tech Stack: Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Sanity CMS with embedded Studio (/studio), next/image with Sanity CDN,
  React 19.

  Design System: Editorial travel-magazine aesthetic — full-bleed hero imagery breaking the container grid, alternating text/image
  sections, Fraunces Variable (display) + DM Sans Variable (body), warm terracotta/forest/cream palette, 800ms staggered crossfades, drop
  caps, pull quotes, tabular numerals.

  Content Architecture: Four Sanity schemas — Room (6 rooms with galleries, amenities, pricing), HomePage (hero, story, featured rooms,
  testimonial, CTA), Testimonial (guest quotes with room references), SiteSettings (singleton for contact, social, SEO, booking config).
  All images support hotspot/crop; Portable Text for rich descriptions.

  Performance & SEO: next/image with proper sizes, priority loading, blur placeholders (LQIP), variable fonts with display: swap. Dynamic
  metadata, Open Graph/Twitter cards, JSON-LD structured data (LodgingBusiness, HotelRoom, ItemList), auto-generated sitemap.xml and
  robots.txt. Target Lighthouse 90+.

  Accessibility: WCAG AA contrast, semantic landmarks, focus-visible styles, ARIA labels, alt text on all images, form validation with
  error announcements.

  Developer Experience: One-time migration script (scripts/migrate-content.mjs) uploads 28 images to Sanity asset store and creates all
  documents idempotently. Mock data fallback for offline development. Zero separate Sanity dev server — Studio embedded at /studio via
  next-sanity.

  Deployment: Vercel (frontend) + npx sanity deploy (Studio hosted at *.sanity.studio). Environment-driven config via .env.local.

title: Bright Smile Dental
description:
Built a performance-focused landing page for a dental practice's teeth whitening consultation campaign. The page drives qualified leads
  through a free consultation offer, combining persuasive copy architecture with technical rigor.

  Stack: Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, deployed on Vercel.

  Architecture: Component-driven composition — Hero, Problem/Benefit, What's Included, Social Proof, Lead Form, Final CTA — each isolated
  and reusable. Variant testing (A/B) is built into the core via URL parameter (?v=a|b), swapping headlines and CTAs server-side with zero
  client-side flicker.

  Tracking & Attribution: First-party UTM capture persists across navigation via sessionStorage, appended to form submissions server-side.
  Dual-pixel tracking (GTM + Meta CAPI) fires deduplicated lead events with enriched payload (variant, UTM, timestamp). Consent-ready
  structure for future CMP integration.

  Lead Pipeline: API route (/api/submit-lead) validates with Zod, rate-limits per IP, forwards to practice CRM via webhook, returns typed
  success/error states — no client-side secrets exposed.

  Performance: Static-first rendering with selective dynamic segments. LCP < 1.8s on 3G. Zero layout shift. Fonts self-hosted via
  next/font. Icons as inline SVG (including the new favicon).

  Accessibility: Semantic HTML, focus-visible states, ARIA labels on form controls, color contrast AA+, reduced-motion respected.

  Result: A maintainable, measurable marketing asset the practice owns — no builder lock-in, no mystery scripts, full data portability.

title: Kindred Coffee Roasters
description:
Kindred Coffee Roasters represents a complete brand-focused redesign and functional transformation of the standard Shopify Dawn theme.
  Rather than a superficial aesthetic change, I built a bespoke e-commerce experience designed to showcase deep Liquid theme development
  and Online Store 2.0 architecture proficiency.

  The project centered on three core requirements: a tactile, warm aesthetic, robust subscription-based functionality, and modular
  flexibility. I moved away from generic templates to build six custom sections—including a high-converting "Build Your Own Bundle"
  builder, a dynamic subscription product page, and a data-driven "Tasting Notes" flavor wheel—all fully configurable via the Shopify Theme
  Editor. By integrating dynamic pricing logic, responsive lifestyle-first imagery, and modular blocks, I created a store that functions
  as a professional, scalable ecosystem for specialty coffee.

  Technically, the project emphasizes performance and maintainability: I utilized optimized Liquid schema settings to prevent hardcoding,
  implemented vanilla JavaScript for lightweight interactive logic, and ensured clean data flow using custom metafields for complex content
  like flavor profiles and brew guides. This portfolio piece demonstrates the ability to solve real-world agency challenges—taking a
  merchant's existing store to the next level through deliberate, purpose-driven development that respects both the brand’s visual identity
  and Shopify’s technical constraints.

---

  To view the live theme, enter 'nullfolio' as the store password.

title: Lumen Salon
description:
Lumen Salon & Spa is a production-ready Next.js 14 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS portfolio piece demonstrating expertise in
  building conversion-focused local business websites that actually rank and convert. The site is architected around a single goal—driving
  appointment bookings—while layering every local SEO trust signal agencies need: consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) across footer,
  contact page, and schema; a complete LocalBusiness JSON-LD with HealthAndBeautyBusiness type, GeoCoordinates, OpeningHoursSpecification,
  and a full OfferCatalog of six services with pricing; Google Maps embed (zero-API-key iframe) and a styled Reviews section mimicking
  Google review cards with static placeholders; and a "Find us on Google" CTA pointing to the real GBP. Booking is handled via Cal.com's
  React embed (@calcom/embed-react), lazy-loaded and styled to feel native, with deep-linking from service cards
  (/book?service=haircut-style) so users land directly on the right event type. The design uses a warm ivory/stone palette with sage accent
  and Cormorant Garamond + Inter typography for an upscale-but-approachable boutique feel, fully responsive and mobile-first with sticky
  header CTAs and click-to-call. Technical highlights include: per-page metadata + Open Graph, sitemap.xml/robots.ts generation, dynamic
  header that's transparent only on the home page, 12-hour time formatting for UX while schema retains 24-hour, custom SVG favicon, and
  environment-driven config for Cal.com namespace and Google Business URL so the demo works instantly but connects to real data on deploy.
  Deployed on Vercel with Lighthouse 90+ targets.
